A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Rubrik’s CUBE. The main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated material and visible omissions in v2’s prompt listings.

before.justification: v1 reports original human and LLM explanation collection, task accuracies, rubric evaluations, inter-rater agreement, and an annotator survey.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds analyses of accuracy by explanation type and individual annotator behavior.

M1.justification: The three nested explanation types, eight quality dimensions, and hierarchical binary scoring remain unchanged. The expanded Section 3.3 clarifies the existing procedure; v1’s Appendix E already requested component-level yes/no judgments rather than an overall quality judgment.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English-language tasks and source datasets: HellaSwag, Logic, RACE, and Write&Improve. The added analyses subdivide existing observations without introducing new tasks, populations, or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The human comparison groups and six LLMs remain unchanged, including in the evaluator-selection comparison. Changing 'Llama 3' to 'Llama 3.1' standardizes the label: Appendix C.2 already identifies Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix C.6 changes the stated Logic few-shot count from six examples to seven. This resolves an inconsistency because v1’s displayed prompt already says seven; it does not establish that experiments were rerun. Dataset selection, sample sizes, model configurations, and agreement metrics are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an analysis relating answer accuracy to explanation type in Figure 2 and Section 5. Figures 8–9 additionally expose individual annotator variation in explanation types and failure dimensions, extending v1’s group-level analyses. Existing survey and answer-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The NASA-TLX boxplots, Friedman testing procedure and significance threshold, and descriptive statistics are retained. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation practices are reported.

E6.justification: Section 5 changes the reported open-/closed-source conciseness-failure percentages from 69.44%/98.18% to 96.89%/99.06%, and the corresponding error-profile plot changes. v1’s Figure 7 disagrees with its prose’s open/closed assignment, so these are reporting revisions, not established performance gains. Accuracy-by-type and individual breakdowns are added; task accuracies and agreement-table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The nested type relation, hierarchical agreement examples, and weighted-F1 class-weight formula in Appendix D are unchanged. Expanded rubric explanations introduce no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the task-independent rubric, approximately 26k-explanation dataset, and two agreement metrics as contributions. The central findings about task-dependent explanation types and conciseness remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new accuracy-by-type patterns and attributes T2’s different behavior to overlapping fallacy labels. Section 4.1.2 and Appendix E newly argue that component-level evaluation mitigates GPT-4o self-preference. The principal limitations concerning binary scoring, English-only data, and confidence assessment are retained.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised resource release with a repository link and reported availability of the dataset, rubric, and code, and supplies the exact NASA-TLX performance question. Conversely, prompt listings in Appendices C and E visibly lose template commands such as loops and block declarations, reducing their direct reproducibility. Most implementation settings were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion covering MQM applications, LLM evaluators, and self-preference, including Li et al. (2025), Brassard et al. (2024), and Panickssery et al. (2024). The distinct TAACO reference is removed. The overarching education-, XAI-, and NLG-based positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 substantially rewrite the framework explanation and scoring instructions, while moving the component-design rationale into Appendix A.1. Section 5 is reorganized into named analytical themes. Together these substantially revise the central exposition; v2 also adds acknowledgments and author contributions.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-page illustrated rubric in Table 6 and individual breakdowns in Figures 8–9, overlays accuracy information on Figure 2, and moves the aggregate failure plot from appendix Figure 7 to main-text Figure 3. Existing tables and accuracy panels are rearranged, Figure 1 is revised, and prompt listings develop visible omissions.

improvement.justification: The explicit scoring instructions, consolidated illustrated rubric, and added accuracy/type and individual-annotator analyses make the largely retained study easier to understand and assess. v2 also reports resource access and aligns its revised conciseness figures with the plot. These gains are tempered by damaged prompt listings and a new self-bias-mitigation claim without a controlled comparison, supporting a limited overall improvement.
